report.summary: Analyzed chunk 4/5 of venders.py; 15 claims checked, 0 broken, 5 uncheckable, 10 kept.

handoff.purpose: Defines AntigravityAdapter, OllamaAdapter, and the available_vendors registry function.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter
symbols.note: Adapter for Google/Antigravity over SSH; disabled until signed_in=True.

symbols.name: OllamaAdapter
symbols.note: Adapter for local or bench Ollama via native /api/chat.

symbols.name: VendorAvailability
symbols.note: Dataclass holding cheap probe result; no model invoked.

symbols.name: available_vendors
symbols.note: Cheap probe function; checks binary existence and Ollama reachability.

claims.text: The prompt goes on STDIN (``agy -p -``) and NEVER on a command line.
claims.why: argv() constructs 'agy', '-p', '-' as separate list elements; stdin_text is passed separately via _runner, confirming STDIN delivery.

claims.text: ``ssh`` with a trailing command does not take an argv: it concatenates its arguments and hands the string to the REMOTE login shell, which re-parses it.
claims.why: argv() includes '--' before 'agy ...', forcing remote shell to treat 'agy' as command, but the docstring warns of shell injection risk; code does not attempt to escape further.

claims.text: this adapter is DISABLED BY DEFAULT: it reports ``unavailable`` / ``not_authenticated`` immediately rather than hanging on an auth prompt.
claims.why: __init__ sets self.signed_in=False by default; _dispatch returns 'unavailable'/'not_authenticated' when not signed_in.

claims.text: An operator asserts sign-in with ``signed_in=True``; nothing here probes it, because probing means invoking a model.
claims.why: signed_in is a boolean parameter; _dispatch checks it without any network probe.

claims.text: The host is passed EXPLICITLY per call. ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is never read for routing and never written
claims.why: Chunk does not show reading or writing OLLAMA_HOST; other code may violate this.

claims.text: ``local`` is ``sensitivity.lane_for_host(host) == "trusted"`` -- numeric loopback only, the same predicate that decides the egress lane, so the two cannot disagree about one host.
claims.why: In __init__, self.local = lane_for_host(self.host) == 'trusted' matches the claim.
_dispatch checks tokens > window and returns error with reason 'over_context_budget' and explanatory stderr.

claims.text: Ollama HEAD-truncates an over-long prompt -- it eats the system prompt first -- so a silently truncated council turn is a reviewer that never saw the question it is answering.
claims.why: Behavior of Ollama server is not observable in this chunk; the claim is about Ollama's internal behavior.

claims.text: The budget is ``_ollama_native.effective_input_window()`` (full ``num_ctx`` minus the generation reserve), reused rather than reinvented.
claims.why: _dispatch calls effective_input_window(reserve) to compute window; matches claim.

claims.text: ONE predicate, shared with the egress gate it feeds. Not a local copy: ``local`` and ``lane`` must never be able to disagree about the same host, and they did (``[::1]`` was local-but-untrusted).
claims.why: self.local is computed from lane_for_host(self.host) == 'trusted'; lane is set via kw.setdefault('lane','trusted') but may be overridden; the comment explains the fix.

claims.text: Does the binary exist; does the Ollama host answer ``/api/version``.
claims.why: Code calls shutil.which for binaries and http_probe(host, path='/api/version') for Ollama.

claims.text: No model is invoked, no prompt is sent, nothing is billed.
claims.why: The function only checks binary existence and HTTP reachability; no model calls.

claims.text: ``agy`` is reported unavailable until an operator asserts sign-in: the only way to test its auth is to call it, and a probe that calls a model is not a probe.
claims.why: Code sets agy_reason to 'not_authenticated' if not agy_signed_in, making available=False.

claims.text: Both callables are injectable so a test can establish availability with no CLI on PATH and no network.
claims.why: Chunk shows 'which' and 'http_probe' as parameters with defaults; injectability is demonstrated but test usage is not shown.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT keyed on host: local 7b and bench 7b are the same weights, so they must collide as one class.
claims.why: independence_class returns ('local', model_family(self.model)); host is not included.

observations.what: available_vendors uses COUNCIL_PROFILES['anthropic'].lane and COUNCIL_PROFILES['openai'].lane; those constants are not defined in this chunk.
available_vendors references shutil.which as default for 'which' parameter; shutil.which is imported.
AntigravityAdapter._dispatch returns 'unavailable' for not_on_path if spawn_error starts with 'not_on_path', but the check uses result.spawn_error.startswith('not_on_path') which is fragile.
OllamaAdapter._dispatch catches ProviderHTTPError and checks for 'timed out' and 'cannot reach' in the error string; these are fragile string matches.
